subject: Recap & next steps — inference latency/throughput hypotheses
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Green <sasha@flinttech.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@flinttech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — inference latency/throughput hypotheses

Hi Sasha / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and the proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key pain points you called out
- Interactive streaming UX feels choppy at peak; users notice token-level stalls during multi-turn chats.
- Non-streaming batch requests occasionally miss p95 latency target during concurrent bursts (end-of-session spikes).
- Cost sensitivity: running many small endpoints for concurrency is getting expensive; looking for predictable unit economics.

Environment you described
- Current stack: SageMaker + Triton for GPU endpoints; some requests go through an API gateway that adds ~15–30ms.
- Model variants: 13B and 70B quantized variants in prod for different workloads.
- Typical window: 200–400 QPS bursty traffic, median request size ~120 tokens.

Success criteria you mentioned
- Streaming p95 under 180ms for the interactive path (end-to-end from request to first tokens streaming).
- Non-stream p95 under 280ms at committed concurrency level.
- Cost per 1k tokens to be competitive with current infra (we discussed a target reduction of ~20%).

Suggested diagnostic probes (what we can run together)
1) Short trial on a dedicated pool to reproduce token stalls (we can provision a small Redwood Dedicated pool for 48 hrs).
2) Collect 1–2 hours of trace-level logs from a low-traffic period: request timestamps, kernel stalls, queue lengths, and first-byte times.
3) Share a 10–20 sample transcript (anonymized) and representative traffic pattern (QPS over a day).

Immediate next steps I propose
- We (Redwood) provision a short trial: 2 GPUs with streaming-enabled runtime and prefix/KV caching turned on — proposed window: Wed 16 Jul, 10:00–16:00 PT.
- Tom/Sasha: send the anonymized traces and a sample transcript by Tue EOD (attached: template for trace fields).
- Karthik/Monica: scope a minimal config for the trial and a capacity matrix so we can map expected p95 at different concurrencies.

I’m copying Karthik and Monica to own the technical tasks below. If that schedule works, I’ll send a calendar invite with the trial details and temporary credentials.

Thanks — looking forward to proving that we can tighten the streaming UX while improving cost.

—
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: token-trace-template.csv (see referenced fields)
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@flinttech.com>

Cc: Sasha Green <sasha@flinttech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — inference latency/throughput hypotheses

Alex —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Streaming p95 goal: we were hoping for <=150ms for first-token in the interactive flows (this is perceived latency for end users). If Redwood can get us under 150ms in the trial, that would be a win.
- Non-stream p95: target is 250–300ms depending on model size; 13B is more sensitive to concurrency here.
- Current infra overhead breakdown (approx): 15–30ms API gateway, 40–60ms network/hop variability, rest is model serving. So we suspect model-serving and KV cache warms are the biggest levers.

We’ll send:
- 30 minutes of anonymized request traces (JSON) and 12 sample chat transcripts by Tue 14 Jul 18:00 PT.
- Prefer the trial window to be Thu 17 Jul morning if possible (we have fewer users then).

On the trial configuration: please keep the trial isolated to a non-prod project and provide a short checklist of what you’ll measure (first-byte, token-spacing, GPU utilization, queue depth).

—
Tom
Director of Product — FlintTech
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Green <sasha@flinttech.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@flinttech.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — inference latency/throughput hypotheses

Quick internal/visible-to-client checklist I drafted — feel free to share with FlintTech: 

Trial measurement checklist (what Redwood will capture)
- First-token latency (end-to-end): breakdown by gateway, network, runtime scheduling, kernel execution.
- Inter-token spacing (real-time streaming): measure jitter per token and aggregate p95 of the gaps.
- Queue depth & backpressure: per-request queuing times and worker occupancy.
- KV cache hit ratio and warmup behavior (prefix hits).
- GPU occupancy, SM utilization, CUDA kernel stalls (if available) and memory pressure.
- Cost delta: tokens served vs GPU-hours used; compute per-1k-token cost estimate for trial.

Proposed probe plan
1) Baseline: ingest their trace and replay at 1/10th scale to sanity-check config.
2) Warmup: run replay at 50% expected QPS for 30m to warm caches.
3) Stress: ramp to target burst QPS (they mentioned 200–400) and measure p95 and tail token jitter.

Deliverables by Redwood after trial
- Short report (p95 breakdown, traces highlighting stalls, recommended config: batching windows, KV cache settings, quantization profile).
- A small recommended capacity matrix (attached spreadsheet) that maps p95 to effective concurrency/GPU count.

Action items
- Alex: confirm trial window with FlintTech (Thu 17 Jul morning preferred).
- Monica: prepare capacity matrix and populate the sample-capacity-matrix.xlsx (attached).
- Tom/Sasha: upload traces and sample transcripts to shared Drive link.

I’ll pre-populate the report template so we can deliver within 48 hours of the trial.

—
Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Green <sasha@flinttech.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@flinttech.com>

Tom / Sasha —

Perfect — thanks for the targets and timeline. We’ll aim for Thu 17 Jul 09:00–13:00 PT for the trial (window booked tentatively). I will send a calendar invite once you confirm the time works. 

Attachments (for the trial): sample-capacity-matrix.xlsx, token-trace-example.json

Immediate asks for you before the trial
- Upload the anonymized traces and sample transcripts to the Drive link in my first email by Wed 15 Jul 18:00 PT.
- Confirm the model variant(s) you want in the trial (13B quantized only, or both 13B + 70B?). If you want both, tell us which traffic split to simulate.

If you confirm the timeslot I’ll also include temporary credentials and a one-page checklist for what to monitor during the run. After the run we’ll produce the p95 breakdown and an action plan to reach your 150ms streaming target.

Best,
Alex
